newsitem.title: UK: LME business slack, prices settle back slightly.
newsitem.headline: LME business slack, prices settle back slightly.

text.p: Early LME trading was slow on Monday, with the market preparing for "third Wednesday" pricing against the June date in the rings later in the day, traders said.
Warehouse stock data, which showed falls in copper and aluminium inventories but no movement in lead and zinc stocks, generally had little impact.
"It has been fairly slow so far...we are just sitting back ahead of the rings," one said.
Copper edged up from $2,570 a tonne, which was seen as fairly important chart support, but the move was just a knee-jerk reaction to an 1,875-tonne stock decline.
Although LME stocks were falling, much of the movement was a simple case of inventory re-distribution, with material moving in to Comex warehouses, some noted.
Three months prices settled at $2,573, down $17 from Friday's kerb close, but basically little different from the late inter-office close.
Aluminium wobbled on some selling ahead of the "third Wednesday" action, with a 3,850-tonne stock fall ignored.
Traders said heavy lending of June/July late last week had defused technical tightness, with cash/threes now back out to $25/27 contango.
Also, a perception remained that the consistent stock falls were not destined for consumption, with metal moving instead in to non-LME stores.
Business was at $1,580 a tonne, down $6 from Friday's kerb close.

Nickel prices were drifting lower, despite the 264-tonne fall in stocks. The continued strike at Inco's Sudbury facilities, and the likelihood that the dispute would continue through the summer maintenance shutdown, was also fading as a supportive factor.
The softer trend might reflect talk of Russian off-warrant metal in Europe and the possibility that Norilsk operations were not being hit by gas power cutbacks. The market was $40 easier at $7,340.
Zinc was $2 higher at $1,376, while lead was $1 softer at $628. Both markets were slow.
Tin was quoted at a slightly soggier $5,545/55 a tonne, while alloy was quoted at $1,465/75 a tonne, also slightly lower.
